summary: The National Housing Emergency Act of 2026 requires the President to declare a national housing emergency and invoke the Defense Production Act to boost residential housing construction and rehabilitation. It suspends certain federal requirements, streamlines environmental reviews, sets minimum residential building codes, and requires state and local governments to meet pro-growth housing rules to receive specific federal block grant funding.

affected_groups.effect: Required by Congress to declare a national housing emergency and invoke the Defense Production Act.
Must meet pro-growth requirements and avoid placing substantial burdens on housing construction through land-use regulations to remain eligible for certain federal block grant funding.
Required to expedite waiver processes under the Build America, Buy America Act and handle grant administration under modified rules.
affected_groups.group: Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and Office of Management and Budget

affected_groups.effect: Impacted by the suspension of various federal regulations, streamlining of environmental reviews, and application of the 2009 International Residential Code or manufactured housing standards during the emergency.

key_provisions: Expresses the sense of Congress that the President should declare a national housing emergency and invoke the Defense Production Act to increase domestic production of materials supporting housing construction and rehabilitation.
Amends the Defense Production Act of 1950 to include residential construction, rehabilitation, and housing within its scope.

Suspends specific statutory requirements and regulations under the Cranston-Gonzalez National Affordable Housing Act and the Community Development Banking and Financial Institutions Act during the national emergency.

Exempts HUD-funded housing preservation or infill projects from federal environmental review requirements and limits projects using multiple federal programs to a single environmental review under the National Environmental Policy Act.
Establishes a 'Pro-Growth Requirement' funding condition for state and local governments receiving federal block grants, requiring positive housing growth and actions to remove development barriers.
Prohibits states and local governments from implementing land-use regulations that place a substantial burden on residential housing construction or rehabilitation during the emergency.
Provides that the emergency terminates on October 1, 2031, or once 4,000,000 additional residential housing units are built or rehabilitated, whichever comes earlier.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact mechanism the President must use outside of the stated sense of Congress provisions.
Detailed funding amounts or appropriations dedicated to the execution of the Defense Production Act authorities for housing.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The National Housing Emergency Act of 2026 requires the President to declare a national housing emergency and invoke the Defense Production Act to boost residential housing construction and rehabilitation. It suspends certain federal requirements, streamlines environmental reviews, sets minimum residential building codes, and requires state and local governments to meet pro-growth housing rules to receive specific federal block grant funding.
summary_detail.significance: The bill targets the national housing shortage by combining presidential emergency powers with broad regulatory relief and federal funding conditions. Its impact involves altering federal housing programs, overriding certain local land-use barriers, changing environmental review processes, and tying federal transportation and community block grants to local housing production growth until 4 million new units are built or October 1, 2031.
